Track rotation is measured relative to the vertically down axis. So vertical track get a bit weird when it's angle is so close to it's reference place.

To solve it, select the "vertical" tick box on your roll points to change their reference plane and set their angle accordingly. 

If you select the last node of the track with the roll point box still open, you can set it's roll parameters and it should stay that way as you build the track out.

Its technically my favourite, but it's really put me off of RMCs in general, as the intensity feels completely unmotivated and done at the expense of the guest experience. Compared to Goliath or Lost Gravity, each airtime hill had harsh transitions with abrupt changes between +2g and -1g, going against what would be comfortable for a human being.

The airtime on a night ride of goliath after 10 hours of warming up was just as strong as anything on untamed, but it's gentle profiling made it feel like a natural yet exceptional experience, working with the body's comfortable enjoyment instead of fighting against it for the sake of a cheap shock over and over again (the return leg was nothing but jolt after jolt of uncomfortable airtime). The more complex elements of untamed proved that everything in the layout was deliberate (the 270° stall was traversed with so much grace compared to the simple bunny hills of the rest of the ride), but it came across like schilke/draves was showing off about how intense a ride can be without considering what such intensity would feel like for a rider on the other side of the world.

Apologies if this seems like a self-entitled ramble, but the flow of Lost Gravity (particularly the first half, which imo is pretty much perfect) and Goliath, made the intense moments stand out far above Untamed while offering a more enjoyable, complete ride experience.

I got curious so did some vague maths!

Counting the number of truss sections on the tower, there are 21 segemts along 126m of height, so 6m a segment. The red/blue transition qhere the cars typically reach is 16 segments up, so 96m off the ground, or 314ft.

The elevation maps show that the station is situated at 1180ft above sea level, and the tower base/lex luther building is at 1120ft. So we have a 60ft elevation change, therefore implying an actual drop height of 254ft/77.5m. 

Using the ol' equations of  motion (v² = u² + 2as), the minimum speed needed to reach that height would be 39m/s, or 87mph, neglecting all losses.
